rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for looking at or paying attention to something.

example.jyutping: ngo5 mui5 jat6 dou1 tai2 din6 si6

rows.note: 手錶 is the all-purpose noun for a portable or wearable timepiece.

example.jyutping: ngo5 maai5 zo2 zek3 san1 sau2 biu1

rows.note: 錶 is the shorter choice when the context already makes clear that a watch is meant.

example.english: What time is it on your watch now?
example.jyutping: nei5 zek3 biu1 ji4 gaa1 gei2 dim2 aa3

rows.note: Use 睇住 when you mean keeping an eye on or guarding a person or belonging.

example.english: You watch my bag for me while I go shopping.
example.traditional: 你幫我睇住個袋，我去買嘢。
example.jyutping: nei5 bong1 ngo5 tai2 zyu6 go3 doi6 ngo5 heoi3 maai5 je5

rows.note: Use 留意 when telling someone to pay attention to a possible immediate danger or hazard.

example.english: Be careful and watch out for that car.
example.jyutping: siu2 sam1 di1 lau4 ji3 zyu6 gaa3 ce1

rows.note: 守更 refers to a guard duty or watch, especially when someone is assigned to keep watch.

example.english: It is my turn to keep watch tonight.
example.jyutping: gam1 maan5 leon4 dou3 ngo5 sau2 gaang1

rows.note: 監視 refers to the surveillance or monitoring aspect of keeping watch rather than physical guard duty.

example.english: The police are keeping watch on that person.
example.traditional: 警方一路監視住嗰個人。
example.jyutping: ging2 fong1 jat1 lou6 gaam1 si6 zyu6 go2 go3 jan4

rows.note: Use 提防 when warning someone to be wary of a person or thing that may cause trouble.

example.english: Watch out for that stranger; they don't seem like a good person.
example.traditional: 提防嗰個陌生人，佢好似唔係好人。
example.jyutping: tai4 fong4 go2 go3 mak6 sang1 jan4 keoi5 hou2 ci5 m4 hai6 hou2 jan4
